newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan governor quits in constitutional row.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan governor quits in constitutional row.

text.p: The first elected governor of Taiwan province, James Soong, resigned on Tuesday in a widening constitutional row over plans by the island's exiled Republic of China government to dismantle his provincial government.

"I have officially tendered my resignation to Chairman Lee and Premier Lien Chan this afternoon," Soong told the provincial assembly in comments broadcast on state radio, referring to President and ruling Nationalist Party chairman Lee Teng-hui.

Moves to radically pare or even eliminate the provincial government got a boost on Saturday when the Nationalists and main opposition Democratic Progressive Party agreed that all elections at the provincial level should be frozen.
They agreed to form a committee to study ways to boost state efficiency and reduce overlapping duties through layoffs -- chiefly at the expense of the huge provincial bureaucracy.
Soong, 54, speaking with great emotion, said he could not accept the task he had been given of orchestrating the streamlining, and particularly the job of halting elections.
"As the first elected governor of Taiwan I have been asked to handle the matter of freezing provincial government elections. This is emotionally unbearable," Soong said.
Since the Nationalists took refuge on Taiwan in 1949 after their defeat by China's communists, the island has had two largely overlapping administrations at the provincial and national level.
